macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer worst session since July
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% for its fifth decline in six sessions, while the Nasdaq dropped 1.9% as artificial-intelligence and semiconductor stocks led the selloff. The Dow declined about 48 points, or 0.1%.[1]

items.title: Hot inflation data raises Fed rate-hike concerns
items.summary: September consumer-price inflation accelerated to 3.7% year over year, above the 3.6% forecast, while producer prices rose 1.3% month over month and 6.3% year over year. The data increased expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates later this year.[3][4]

items.title: Fed official signals another rate hike may be appropriate
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said he sees one more interest-rate increase as appropriate this year, adding to pressure on rate-sensitive technology shares.[4]

items.title: Asian technology stocks plunge amid global AI selloff
items.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI fell about 8% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.9% as investors reassessed high technology valuations and the impact of higher rates. Nasdaq futures were also lower in early trading.[2]

items.title: TSMC reports strong earnings despite technology-sector selloff
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and indicated that capital expenditure would increase over the next two years, but its U.S.-listed shares still fell about 2.5% amid the broader semiconductor selloff.[2][8]

items.title: Bank earnings produce mixed market reaction
items.summary: Bank of America shares fell nearly 5% after earnings were affected by a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty, while BlackRock shares rose after beating third-quarter analyst expectations. Morgan Stanley also reported results as financial-sector earnings continued.[4]

items.title: ASML raises outlook on strong AI demand
items.summary: Chip-equipment maker ASML reported record third-quarter sales and raised its full-year outlook, citing continued demand linked to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.[4]

items.title: Retail sales remain resilient
items.summary: U.S. retail sales rose 0.8% in September after a revised 1.3% increase in August, exceeding expectations and suggesting consumer demand remained firm despite elevated inflation.[3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $82,000 as hot inflation data triggers crypto sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin declined about 2.6% in 24 hours to roughly $81,150, while Ethereum fell 5.2%, Dogecoin 4.8%, and XRP 3.7%. The broader crypto market lost about 3% as stronger-than-expected inflation increased expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike.[1]

items.title: Nearly $1 billion in crypto positions liquidated
items.summary: About 173,758 traders were liquidated for approximately $929 million over 24 hours, with long positions accounting for most losses. Bitcoin later stabilized near $82,000 as Treasury yields eased.[2]

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs record sizable outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw approximately $261.5 million in net outflows, while spot Ether ETFs recorded about $129.5 million in outflows, adding pressure to already weak crypto markets.[2]

items.title: EU classifies USDC as first significant e-money token under MiCA
items.summary: The European Banking Authority designated Circle’s USDC as the first significant e-money token under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets framework. The designation brings enhanced reserve oversight and supervision for large stablecoins.[3]

items.title: Trump crypto adviser departs as U.S. CLARITY Act vote stalls
items.summary: White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt reportedly left without an announced successor, while the CLARITY Act remained short of the votes needed for Senate passage. The leadership change adds uncertainty to the administration’s crypto legislative agenda.[4]

items.title: Starknet votes on potential transition to independent Layer 1
items.summary: Starknet launched a seven-day governance vote to consider becoming an independent Layer 1 blockchain rather than continuing as an Ethereum-based network.[5]

items.title: Polygon completes Coinme acquisition
items.summary: Polygon Labs completed its acquisition of regulated crypto exchange Coinme, expanding its Open Money Stack payments platform to 48 U.S. states through money-transmitter licenses, exemptions, and federal registration.[6]

items.title: Walrus token surges after Sui-linked AI data integration
items.summary: WAL rose about 47% in 24 hours after the DATA Foundation announced that its AI training-data registry and applications would join the Sui ecosystem, using Walrus as the default storage layer.[6]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open open-weight model
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter multimodal model with about 42 billion active parameters and a context window of roughly 1 million tokens. Meta says it targets long-horizon tasks, software engineering and multi-step reasoning, and can run in quantized form across linked Apple Mac Studios.

items.title: Google expands access to Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google reportedly opened Gemini 4 Argon to paid API users, Google AI Studio, Antigravity Ultra and eligible Gemini subscribers. The model is positioned for long-horizon coding, enterprise workflows and cyber defense, with introductory API pricing scheduled to increase after November 30.

items.title: Liquid AI launches LFM2.5-24B-A2B
items.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, an open-weight reasoning model with 24 billion total parameters and 2 billion active parameters. The release is aimed at efficient on-device and agent applications.

items.title: JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 coding model
items.summary: JetBrains released Mellum2.1, a 12-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 2.5 billion active parameters. The model was trained with reinforcement learning in real-world environments and is available under the Apache 2.0 license.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate concealed model backdoors
items.summary: A reported NeurIPS 2026 paper describes methods for embedding encrypted networks inside model weights that activate only after a secret trigger. In a small chemistry proof of concept, the hidden capability reportedly resisted fine-tuning and weight-noising defenses.

items.title: Nvidia announces European investment and UK safety compute
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced $2 billion in European investments and pledged $250 million in compute for UK AI safety and security research. The initiative emphasizes open-weight models and support for European AI startups.

items.title: New analysis finds limited safety reporting among Chinese AI releases
items.summary: SemiAnalysis reviewed 857 releases from nine Chinese developers and found that only 3.6% had a developer-published safety result, while 1.1% had one available at or before launch. The analysis reported a median delay of 42 days for safety results published after release.

items.title: Google AI Edge releases ML Drift inference engine
items.summary: Google AI Edge released ML Drift, a cross-platform GPU inference engine supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU. The project is intended to broaden deployment options for machine-learning workloads across devices and platforms.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Valor Mortis launches on PC and current-generation consoles
items.summary: One More Level’s action game Valor Mortis reportedly releases today on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S, and joins Game Pass.

items.title: Gran Turismo 7 Spec IV update launches
items.summary: Sony announced the launch of Gran Turismo 7’s Spec IV Part 1 update, alongside a first look at a Gran Turismo limited-edition DualSense controller.

items.title: Brazil expands public support for game development
items.summary: Brazil’s government signed regulations recognizing video games as audiovisual and cultural products, enabling access to public funding and announcing additional support for startups, education, and a national games platform.

items.title: 007 First Light dated for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: IO Interactive reportedly set the Nintendo Switch 2 release of 007 First Light for March 18, 2027, and showed footage of the hybrid-console version.

items.title: Bryson Tiller reveals Brutal Industry game
items.summary: Musician Bryson Tiller shared details about Brutal Industry, a beat-’em-up inspired by the music business that he is developing through Trapsoul Games for Arcade1Up cabinets, with a planned 2027 release.

items.title: Brazilian games industry spending growth highlighted at GCAP 2026
items.summary: A GCAP 2026 presentation cited annual global video-game spending growth of roughly 11.4%, as industry discussions focused on common assumptions about the sector.
